title: Give 155 unnamed rows the name Lichess uses for the same position
description: 2,144 of 5,899 rows carry no alternative name at all, which is the catalogue's largest gap: a reader searching the name their own source uses does not find us. This closes the part that needs no research. Every row here cross-references lichess-org/chess-openings by EXACT position, so the Lichess string names the same thing rather than an ancestor, and it is what millions of players see. Four filters: no existing alias; exact position match only, because a prefix match names a shallower line and would give dozens of rows one alias; the name must identify exactly one row in the whole cross-reference, because Lichess reuses names; no ASCII-folded eponym, because the catalogue's diacritic rule forbids them; and nothing that is already another row's canonical name or alias, which the registrar guard rejects. 2,105 rows differ from their Lichess name, 367 by exact match, 186 uniquely, and 155 survive every filter. The 30 held back are a policy question, not a data one: see docs/evidence/provenance/lichess-alias-import.md.
